Rashi on Chullin 38a:10:1.hebrew: בתחלת שחיטה - כלומר, אפי' פירכסה בתחלת שחיטה, דייה, כשרה, אע"ג דהויא מסוכנת, כיון דמלאים כותלי בית השחיטה דם, בידוע שזינקה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:10:1.english: At the beginning of the slaughter - That is to say, even if it convulsed at the beginning of the slaughter, that is sufficient, and it is kosher, even though it is dangerously ill; since the walls of the slaughterhouse are filled with blood, it is known that it spurted.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:1.hebrew: וכמידת ר"א - דאמר זינוק הוי פירכוס:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:1.english: And according to the standard of R. Elazar - Who said that a spurt [of blood] is a [sign of] convulsion.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:2.hebrew: ואמר שמואל כו' - להכי איצטריך לפרושי דכותלים דהכא לא הוו כותלים ממש, אלא כותלי בית השחיטה. דאי הוו כותלים ממש, למחר היינו יכולים להבין אי האי זינוק הוה בתחלת שחיטה או באמצע שחיטה: דאי הוה בתחלת שחיטה, ימצא הזינוק למעלה בכותל, דמחמת כח וחיות שהיה עדיין בבהמה זינקה למרחוק. ואם ימצא הזינוק למטה בכותל, בידוע שבאמצע שחיטה זינקה, שלא היה בה כח כל כך לזנק הדם למרחוק. אבל השתא דאמר שמואל דהני כותלי לא הוו כותלי ממש אלא כותלי בית השחיטה, לא מצינו למידע אי תחלת שחיטה זינקה או לאחר שחיטה. ולהכי קאמר "אי אמרת בשלמא כל כמה דפירכס", אפילו בתחלת שחיטה הוי פירכוס:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:2.english: And Shmuel said, etc. - This is why it was necessary to explain that the "walls" here are not actual walls, but the walls of the slaughterhouse. For if they were actual walls, the next day we would be able to tell whether this spurting occurred at the beginning of the slaughter or in the middle of the slaughter. If it was at the beginning of the slaughter, the spurt would be found high up on the wall, since because of the strength and vitality that was still in the animal, it spurted [the blood] far away. But if the spurt would be found low on the wall, it is known that it spurted in the middle of the slaughter, when it no longer had so much strength to spurt the blood far away. But now that Shmuel has said that these walls are not actual walls but the walls of the slaughterhouse, we cannot know whether it spurted at the beginning of the slaughter or after the slaughter. And this is why [Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak] says, "Granted, if you say [that it means] for as long as it convulses," [then] even at the beginning of the slaughter it counts as convulsing.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:3.english: It is well - For we see the next day, through the spurting [of the blood], that it convulsed in the evening.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:4.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת - באמצע שחיטה בעינן, מאן לימא לן למחר דזינוק דלאורתא באמצע שחיטה הוה? דלמא בתחלת שחיטה זניק:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:11:4.english: But if you say - [that the spurting must occur] in the middle of the slaughter, [then] we require this. Who will tell us tomorrow that the spurting of the evening occurred in the middle of the slaughter? Perhaps it spurted at the beginning of the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:12:1.hebrew: ודלמא - לעולם שאר פירכוסין לא הוו פירכוס אלא באמצע או בגמר שחיטה, ושאני זינוק דעדיף חיותיה, ופירכוס גדול הוא, הלכך אפילו בתחלת שחיטה זינקה שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:12:1.english: But perhaps - Actually, other convulsions are not considered a convulsion [that permits the animal] unless they occur in the middle of the slaughter or at its end. But leaping is different, since its vitality is greater and it is a large convulsion. Therefore, even if it leapt at the beginning of the slaughter, it is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:13:1.hebrew: דייה אם זינקה - ומדקתני "דייה", מכלל דקיל:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:13:1.english: It is sufficient if it spurted - And from the fact that [the mishna] teaches "it is sufficient," it is implied that [spurting] is a lenient [sign].

Rashi on Chullin 38a:13:2.hebrew: קיל מדרבן גמליאל - דבעי ביד וברגל בשניהם:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:13:2.english: It is more lenient than Rabban Gamliel - For [Rabban Gamliel] requires [a movement] of the foreleg and the hind leg, both of them.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:13:3.english: And it is superior to [the sign of] the Rabbis - For they say [that it suffices if the animal moves] its foreleg or its hind leg.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:14:1.english: Avubram - [This is] the name of the man.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:14:2.hebrew: אבוה בר אבוברם - זהו אבוברם עצמו, ומכירין היו את הבן ולא את האב, והיו קורין אותו על שם בנו, שעשו את בנו סימן לו:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:14:2.english: Avuha bar Avuram - This is Avuram himself. They knew the son but not the father, and they would call him by his son's name, because they made his son an identifying sign for him.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:14:3.hebrew: עד - משמע דחמיר האי פירכוס דרבנן מהנך דלעיל. ואי דר"א עדיף, מאי עד דרבנן? משמע דעדיף! כיון מיבעי להו למימר, אלא ש"מ זינוק קיל, ואפ"ה סגיא ליה כי הוי בתחלת שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:14:3.english: Until - This implies that this convulsion of the Rabbis is more stringent than those mentioned above. But if R. Elazar's [statement] is the more stringent one, then what is the Rabbis' "until"? It implies that theirs is the more stringent! Since they needed to say [it], rather, learn from this that a jerk (zinuk) is lenient, and even so it suffices when it occurs at the beginning of the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:17:1.hebrew: בסוף שחיטה - סוף ממש, שתפרכס בגמר שחיטה, דתהוי בה חיות אחר שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:17:1.english: At the end of the slaughter - The very end, that it convulses upon the completion of the slaughter, [for] there is life in it after the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:1.hebrew: גועה והטילה ריעי - או זה או זה. גועה, צועקת, כמו "אם יגעה שור על בלילו" (איוב ו׳:ה׳):
Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:1.english: Bellowing and excreting loose waste - Either this or that. "Bellowing" means crying out, like "or will the ox low over its fodder?" (Job 6:5).

Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:2.hebrew: לאבא - לרב הוה קרי ליה שמואל הכי, משום כבוד:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:2.english: To Abba - Shmuel would call Rav by this name [Abba] out of respect.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:3.hebrew: לאזוזי אוני - לפרכס האוזן, בתמיה, דפירכוס חיות גדול הוא זה. אזוזי לשון מזיזין אותו ממקומו (אבות פ"ג מי"ז):
Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:3.english: To move the ear - To twitch the ear. [This is said] as a rhetorical question: Is this a great sign of life, [that it should count as] twitching? The word "azuzei" is an expression of "moving it from its place" (Avot 3:17).

Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:4.hebrew: שאני אומר - שאינה צריכה כל כך, אלא כל פירכוס שמסוכנת מפרכסת, שאינה עושה דבר שהוא הוצאת נפש, הוי פירכוס, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:1:4.english: For I say - That it [the animal] does not need so much [i.e., that it does not need to perform all these movements]. Rather, any convulsion of a dangerously ill animal that convulses, [even if] it does not do anything that is an expulsion of life, counts as a convulsion, as [the Gemara] will state below.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:2:1.hebrew: שאין המיתה עושה - בשעת הוצאת נפש קרי לה מתה, ובבהמה דקה קאי, דאילו גסה אפילו כפופה ופשטתה הוי פירכוס:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:2:1.english: That death does not cause - At the time of the departure of the soul, [the Gemara] calls it "dying." And [this statement] refers to a small animal, for with a large animal, even if it was bent and then stretched out, it is [considered] convulsing.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:4:1.hebrew: אי - מדוקיא דמתניתין הוה גמרינן לה כדקדייקת: הא החזירה כשרה משמע, שפשטתה מכפיפותה והחזירה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:4:1.english: If - From the inference of our mishna we would have learned it as you infer: "If she returned it, it is valid" implies that she extended it from its bent position and then returned it.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:4:2.english: But extended - [If it was extended] from the beginning and she then bent it, [I would say it is] not [a convulsion].

Rashi on Chullin 38a:4:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - דהיכא דהויא פשוטה מעיקרא וכפפתה, הוי פירכוס:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:4:3.english: It teaches us - That where it was extended originally and it bent it, this is [considered] convulsing.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:5:1.english: In his name - Of Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:1.hebrew: הא - דאמר רב לעיל: גועה הוי פירכוס:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:1.english: This - For Rav said above that bellowing constitutes convulsing.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:2.hebrew: דעבי קלה - שהיה קולה עבה וחזקה, דודאי אתי מכח חיות:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:2.english: That its voice is thick - That its voice was thick and strong, for it certainly comes from the power of life.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:3.hebrew: דעמי קלה - כהה, מתרגמינן "עמיא" (ויקרא יג):
Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:3.english: Dimmed (da'ami) light - Dark; we translate [the word "kehah" as] "amya" (Leviticus 13).

Rashi on Chullin 38a:6:5.english: Spurts - To a distance, and this is [a sign of] life.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:7:1.english: Rav Chisda said: The convulsion that they mentioned - "I heard it [said] at the end of the slaughter." And I explain: What is the "end" that I heard? It is the middle of the slaughter. And the reason he calls it "end" is to exclude the case where the animal convulsed at the beginning of the slaughter: since it did not convulse in the middle of the slaughter, it does not have this kind of vitality, and [an animal] like this is forbidden because of the taking of life.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:1.hebrew: מנא אמינא לה - דהאי "סוף" ששמעתי, "אמצע" הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:1.english: From where do I say this? - That this "end" that I heard [i.e., "convulsion at the end of the slaughter"] is [actually] the "middle."

Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:2.hebrew: אימת - פשטה ולא החזירה, דאמרינן פסולה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:2.english: When? - [When] it extended [its foreleg] and did not return it, concerning which we say that it is unfit.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:3.hebrew: כל היכי תיחי ותיזיל - דלאחר ששחטה לא תסגי בפשיטת יד בלא כפיפה וחזרה, בתמיה:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:8:3.english: All the more so, [that] she should live and go - [Meaning:] that after he slaughtered her, an extension of the foreleg without bending and returning it will not suffice [to count as a sign of life]? [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:9:1.hebrew: א"ל רבא לעולם סוף שחיטה - דוקא. ודקאמרת כל היכי תיחי ותיזיל, לאחר שחיטה שתפשוט ותחזיר:
Rashi on Chullin 38a:9:1.english: Rava said to him: Actually, [it is] at the end of the slaughter - Specifically. And as for what you said, [that] however [the animal] may live and go on [walking], [my answer is that the *pirkus* applies] after the slaughter, [meaning that the animal] extends [its foreleg] and draws it back.

Rashi on Chullin 38a:9:2.hebrew: שאני אומר כל שאינה עושה כן - פשטה וחזרה לאחר שחיטה, בידוע כו':
Rashi on Chullin 38a:9:2.english: For I say that any [animal] that does not do so - Extend [its leg] and return [it] after slaughter, it is known, etc.

Tosafot on Chullin 38a:1:1.hebrew: גועה או הטילה ריעי וכשכשה באזנה ה"ז פירכוס - אפילו לר"ג דמחמיר ובעי פירכוס יד ורגל, חשיב האי פירכוס. ולהכי פריך שפיר מברייתא דקתני בסמוך גועה והטילה ריעי אין זה פירכוס, ושמואל דאמר איצטריך ליה לאבא אזוזי אוני סבר כרבנן דאמרי או יד או רגל. ולהכי פריך עליה דרב ענן דמפרש מילתיה דשמואל תנינא, דפשיטא דאליבא דרבנן פשוטה וכפפה ה"ז פירכוס, כפופה ופשטה לא הוי פירכוס:
Tosafot on Chullin 38a:1:1.english: If it bellowed, or excreted loose dung, or wagged its ear, this is a convulsion - Even according to Rabban Gamliel, who is stringent and requires a convulsion of the hand and the leg, this counts as a convulsion. And therefore [the Gemara] objects properly from the baraita that teaches nearby, "If it bellowed and excreted loose dung, this is not a convulsion." And Shmuel, who said "Abba needed to move the ears," holds like the Rabbis, who say [that a convulsion is] either the hand or the leg. And therefore [the Gemara] objects to Rav Anan, who explains Shmuel's statement [by saying], "We learned [this in the Mishnah]," for it is obvious, according to the Rabbis, that [if it] extended [its leg] and bent it, this is a convulsion, [whereas if it] bent it and extended it, it is not a convulsion.

Tosafot on Chullin 38a:1:2.hebrew: אצטריך ליה לאבא - פי' בקונטר', דשמואל הוה קרי הכי לרב בלשון כבוד. ובערוך פירש שכך שמו, ורב היו קורין אותו על שם חשיבותו, כמו דבכל דוכתי הוו קרו ליה רבי לר' יהודה הנשיא, ושמואל שהיה חבירו היה קורהו בשמו. וכן לקמן, אי הכי אמר אבא לא ידע בטרפות כלום; ובערבי פסחים (פסחים דף קיט:) גבי גוזלייא וארזילייא לאבא; ובפרק כל גגות (עירובין דף צד.) אי קפיד אבא קטרו ביה המיינא. ובפירוש משמע סוף פרק ראשית הגז (לקמן חולין דף קלז:), דאמר רבי יוחנן לאיסי, מאן ריש סדרא בבבל, א"ל אבא אריכא, וכעס עליו ר' יוחנן על שקראו כן; משמע בהדיא דאבא לאו לשון חשיבות. ומיהו, ממה שהיה קורהו בשמו לחודיה לא היה כועס, אי לאו משום דאמר אריכא, שזהו לשון גנאי; דר' יוחנן גופיה היה קורהו אבא בפרק כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין פד.), אבא ממשפחת בריאים הוה, אע"פ שרב היה חשוב הרבה מר' יוחנן. מיהו על רב המנונא דאמר בפ' יה"כ (יומא דף פז.) קא אזיל אבא למיקטל גברא, קשה, שהיה תלמידו וקורהו בשמו; ואמר בחלק (סנהדרין ק.) מפני מה היה נענש גחזי, מפני שקורהו לרבו בשמו. ולפירוש הקונט' דאבא לשון חשיבות, ניחא:
Tosafot on Chullin 38a:1:2.english: It was necessary for him [to say it] to Abba - Rashi (the Kuntres) explained that Shmuel would call Rav thus ("Abba") as a term of honor. But the Arukh explained that this was [Rav's] actual name, and that they would call him "Rav" on account of his importance, just as everywhere they called Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi "Rabbi," whereas Shmuel, who was [Rav's] colleague, would call him by his name. And so too below: "If so, Abba does not know anything at all about terefot"; and in Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 119b), regarding "gozalayya and arzilayya are for Abba"; and in the chapter Kol Gagot (Eruvin 94a), "If Abba is particular, tie the mayna to it." And it is explicitly implied at the end of the chapter Reishit HaGez (below, Chullin 137b), where Rabbi Yohanan said to Isi, "Who is the head of the academy in Babylonia?" He said to him, "Abba Arikha," and Rabbi Yohanan became angry with him for calling [Rav] so. This implies explicitly that "Abba" is not a term of importance. However, [Rabbi Yohanan] would not have been angry over his calling [Rav] by his name alone, were it not that he said "Arikha," which is a term of disparagement; for Rabbi Yohanan himself would call him "Abba," in the chapter Kisui HaDam (below, Chullin 84a): "Abba was from the family of Beriim," even though Rav was much greater than Rabbi Yohanan. But regarding Rav Hamnuna, who said in the chapter Yom HaKippurim (Yoma 87a), "Abba is going to kill a man," [this is] difficult, since [Rav] was his teacher and he called him by his name; and it says in [the chapter] Chelek (Sanhedrin 100a), "Why was Gehazi punished? Because he called his master by his name." But according to the explanation of the Kuntres that "Abba" is a term of importance, it is well:

Tosafot on Chullin 38a:8:1.hebrew: אילימא בסוף שחיטה כל היכי תיחי ותיזיל - ומפרש רבינו תם, דמדקתני "שאינה אלא הוצאת נפש", דייק: דאטו מי לא חיתה הרבה אם לא הוציאה נפשה עד סוף שחיטה?:
Tosafot on Chullin 38a:8:1.english: If you say [that it refers to] the end of the slaughter, how could it live and go on? - And Rabbeinu Tam explains that from the fact that it teaches "that it is nothing but the expulsion of the soul," it infers: Would it not have lived for a long time, if it had not expelled its soul until the end of the slaughter?

Tosafot on Chullin 38a:9:1.hebrew: רבא אמר פירכוס שאמרו בסוף שחיטה - והא דלא חיישינן דלמא בתחלת שחיטה זינק, משום דלא שכיחא שיהיה זינוק אלא בסוף:
Tosafot on Chullin 38a:9:1.english: Rava said: The convulsion (pirkus) that they spoke of is at the end of the slaughter - And the reason we are not concerned that perhaps it spurted at the beginning of the slaughter is that it is not common for there to be a spurt except at the end.
